visualTypes.purpose: Show relationships among components, systems, causes, or ideas.
Show diagnostic sequences, decisions, procedures, or workflows.
Compare specifications, symptoms, evidence, tools, causes, or procedures.
Compare quantities, performance, frequencies, results, or measurements.
Show sequence over time, system events, maintenance intervals, or test progression.
Combine concise text, icons, numbers, and relationships into one instructional summary.
Show meaningful parts of a whole only when that relationship is instructionally necessary.

coreRules.rule: Every content block and visual must map to at least one learning objective.
Concepts, terminology, processes, and evidence patterns must be taught before they are assessed.
Knowledge, procedural application, evidence interpretation, and diagnostic reasoning must be distinguished.
Lessons should progress from system understanding to guided interpretation to independent application.
Examples and activities should use realistic symptoms, measurements, tools, documentation, and diagnostic decisions.
Technical instructional claims must be supported by an approved source with provenance preserved.
Vehicle-specific values, procedures, service limits, and specifications must come from an appropriate authoritative source.
General principles must be distinguished from vehicle-specific procedures and specifications.
Visuals must explain, compare, sequence, summarize, or support a learning or diagnostic decision.
Lessons should avoid introducing unnecessary simultaneous concepts, measurements, procedures, and terminology.
Unfamiliar technical terminology must be defined at first instructional use.
Worked examples should precede comparable independent problems or diagnostic tasks.
Lessons should include low-stakes checks before learners advance to more complex tasks.
Feedback must explain why a response or decision is correct or incorrect.
Wrong-answer feedback should address the misconception represented by the response when known.
Assessment items must be answerable from taught content or evidence supplied to the learner.
Assessment difficulty must align with the learning objective and taught cognitive level.
Multiple representations should be used only when each adds instructional value.
Visual and interactive content must include equivalent text, keyboard access, clear headings, and must not rely on color alone.
Lessons must follow the canonical lesson structure unless a documented instructional rationale justifies an exception.

governanceRules: Curriculum classification and academic level remain separate fields.
Draft curriculum remains labeled draft until reviewed.
Approved instructional content and approved assessment content remain separate states.
No scored item becomes available solely because it exists in storage.
Every scored assessment item requires provenance, review status, and curriculum mapping.
Training may include richer coaching and feedback than scored assessment.
Scored assessment must not expose answer-revealing training metadata.
Content changes must be versioned so historical attempts can resolve the curriculum and item versions used.
